newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: ICRC transport Taleban dead to Kabul.
newsitem.headline: ICRC transport Taleban dead to Kabul.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) took the bodies of 14 Taleban fighters to Kabul from opposition territory north of the capital on Saturday.
A press release said: "The ICRC organised the transfer of 14 mortal remains of Taleban soldiers from the Charikar area (60 km or 40 miles north of Kabul) to the military hospital in Kabul.
"This first transfer is a result of negotiations held, at the ICRC intitiative, between belligerent parties. The ICRC started to collect the buried bodies on 8 November in the Charikar area."
Another transfer of bodies could take place shortly.
The Charikar area was the scene of fierce fighting between the radical Taleban militia and forces of the ousted government's top military commander, Ahmed Shah Masood.
When the Taleban took Kabul in late September they moved rapidly north, taking Charikar and pushing Masood into his native Panjsheer valley.
Masood counter-attacked on October 10 and re-took Charikar in heavy fighting. There are no reliable estimates of casualties.
The Taleban and forces loyal to Masood and his ally, the northern leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, are currently fighting on a front line some 20 to 25 kilometers (15 to 19 miles) north of Kabul.
There were heavy exchanges of artillery and rocket fire on the front line nn Saturday morning.
Clashes also occurred between the Taleban and Dostum's forces in the northwestern provinces of Badghis and Faryab.

The return of dead bodies is an important part of Afghan warfare. During the fierce factional fighting that split Kabul for more than four years, temporary ceasefires were regularly negotiated to assist the transfer.
Although elders were generally used to transfer the bodies, journalists -- who regularly crossed the front lines -- were also requested to carry the remains.
